headline: Meta and Microsoft are cutting back how much their own staff use Anthropic's Claude AI and steering them to other tools, including their own.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score of 6: two very large customers cutting back is notable for Anthropic, but the figures come from a single report with unnamed sources.
importance_line: What changed is that two of Anthropic's biggest corporate customers are reported to be using less of its AI in their own offices, which matters to the staff being moved to other tools, then to Anthropic, whose fast growth the report says this challenges, then to Microsoft and Meta, which are promoting their own tools, and the doubt is that the figures come from unnamed sources, cover only internal use, and layoffs and cost-cutting explain part of the fall.
summary: The Information reports, as relayed by The Decoder and Investing.com, that Microsoft, which had projected spending at least $1 billion a year on Anthropic's technology for its own staff, has cut that spending by more than a third and told employees to use its own tools, such as GitHub Copilot, and OpenAI's models instead, and that the number of Meta employees using the Claude Code programming assistant has fallen from about 60,000 to about 30,000, partly because of layoffs and partly because Meta is pushing its own tools, Muse Code and MetaCode. The cuts cover the companies' own use, and the report says customers' spending on Anthropic models through Microsoft's platforms is still growing; The Decoder adds that Meta spent more than $105 million on Claude Code in one 28-day stretch.
notes: The Information's own article is paywalled; its public preview confirms the opening and the 5 Oct 2026 date. Text read on The Decoder (the pool item) and Investing.com via Yahoo Finance, which both relay it. The Decoder's own commentary (cost savings, Anthropic turning into a competitor) is the outlet's view and is not used as fact. Not used: The Decoder's per-employee monthly budget figures, which look doubtful.
